P-1.rule: Preserve a future-safe contribution boundary, but do not build a marketplace, public lifecycle parity, extension discovery service, or ecosystem governance depth for v1.
P-1.doesNotMean: The internal boundary may be vendor-coupled or that untrusted code is admitted.

P-2.rule: Contributions are narrow producers or data-only rules/profiles. They never own root commands, policy, persistence, rendering, termination, or host lifecycle.
P-2.milestoneRequirement: The first vertical slice requires bundled algorithms, bundled TypeScript/Rust providers, and bundled declarative rules only; external distribution/lifecycle is not an exit gate.

A1-RI-04.rule: The CI/non-interactive profile does not load or resolve layer-4 analysis-affecting untracked overrides. Their presence is not an admission failure. Local interactive runs may use layer 4 only when its values and provenance enter PlanId and the explain projection.
A1-RI-04.why: This prevents an unreviewed local file from changing CI without turning mere file presence into a CI denial-of-service switch.

VER-PIVOT-COST.rule: A detector pivot runs only when a detector major changes and a baseline/gate comparison is explicitly requested. Ordinary analysis never invokes it. An unavailable pivot is INDETERMINATE, never attributed to code.
VER-PIVOT-COST.milestoneRequirement: Optional for the first vertical-slice exit.
VER-PIVOT-COST.evidencePosture: Affordability remains UNMEASURED; no cheap/free claim is authorized.

PUBLIC-RULE-IR.rule: The rule IR may be an internal versioned implementation contract, but v1 makes no public compatibility promise for third-party rule authors.
PUBLIC-RULE-IR.revisitWhen: P-1 changes to an explicit ecosystem-depth commitment.

SUPPORT-WINDOWS.rule: The VERSIONING support-window counts remain usable architecture defaults only when consumer-facing material labels them provisional/GUESSED. They are not SLAs and their empirical correctness is not an architecture-freeze blocker.
SUPPORT-WINDOWS.evidencePosture: NOT DISCHARGED until real adoption and compatibility evidence exists.

G3-SUBSTRATE.rule: Rust host/core, bundled TypeScript provider, bundled exactly pinned rustc_driver sidecar, full default install profile, finite supported-platform matrix, and offline assets are the v1 substrate defaults.
G3-SUBSTRATE.evidencePosture: Architecture binding does not qualify or demonstrate the release lanes.

CD-RT-5.attributionProvenance: The product authority was asked, in session on 2026-08-05, how this decision should be attributed, and chose its git identity 'sfbreen' over a full name. The coordinator did not select or infer either field. This matters because section 4.4 is this corpus's forensic record of a fabricated authority attribution, and check-product-dispositions-v2.py FAILS on a bracketed placeholder in either field precisely so that an unfilled amendment can never read as a taken decision.
CD-RT-5.question: Accept or replace the V10/retention architecture candidate's default durable-custody posture, including whether any durable retention is implicit.

decision.boundedRetention: Retention is bounded. The bounds are configurable per project.
decision.dimensionsAreIndependent: Disabling one dimension must not disable another. The shipping product's size bound is parasitic on its count bound and silently deletes nothing when count pruning is off; that defect is explicitly not adopted.
decision.whatFiringABoundDoes: A bound firing transitions the affected record to the EXISTING PURGED state. It is not a deletion model. The record remains addressable, its recordCasRef is retained, and effective capability degrades.
decision.tombstonesSurvive: A tombstone outlives the bytes it describes. Absence is therefore always explainable, and 'purged under policy' is never indistinguishable from 'never existed'.
decision.reasonCodeRequired: A PURGED state must carry why: aged out, size pressure, count pressure, or user request.

defaultPosture.meaning: A project with no configured retention policy retains durably and unboundedly. A durable-authoritative request with no policy PROCEEDS AND WRITES rather than refusing.
defaultPosture.consequenceStatedPlainly: The tool writes analysis evidence into a user's project before that user has been asked. This is the intended behaviour, not a side effect.

overridesAStandingArchitecturalRecommend.recommendation: retention-tiers.v22#recommendedDefaultPosture, verbatim: 'no managed durable user-derived write without an explicit project storage and retention policy', whenPolicyMissing 'advisory/ephemeral only, or reject durable/authoritative evidence request', status AWAITING-PRODUCT-DISPOSITION.
overridesAStandingArchitecturalRecommend.whyThatIsLegitimate: The recommendation's own status was AWAITING-PRODUCT-DISPOSITION. Architecture recommends; the product authority decides; the authority is not bound by the preference. This is the mechanism working, and it is recorded as an override rather than an oversight precisely so a later reader cannot mistake it for one.

defaultPosture.whatItOverturns: retention-tiers.v24 Part A rests on the opposite premise. hasNoDefaultField, absenceIsADistinctState and the ABSENT posture state no longer hold, and all three noAskCases lose their refusal paths — CI's REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE, case 2's REFUSE-TO-START-UNTIL-ANSWERED, and case 3's write-no-policy-on-dismissal are moot once a default exists. Repair belongs in retention-tiers.v25.
defaultPosture.whatSurvives: Freeze law 14 still forbids silent demotion — the default removes the NEED to refuse, not the prohibition on quietly doing less than asked. Purge remains degradation rather than deletion. Tombstones survive. Bounds remain independent.
